clue.text: Trunk of green wood, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the clue phrase is to be spoken and the entry is a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: on a bowling green each ball is called a wood, or bowl

explanation.surface: A remark about a tree trunk of unseasoned timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green wood' looks like unseasoned timber, but it is a wood (ball) used on a bowling green, a BOWL. 'it's said' gives the soundalike, BOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bole is the main stem of a tree below its branches.

clue.text: Yes, put boat out-it's a pretty place to see

definitions.text: it's a pretty place to see

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Agreeing to launch a boat at a scenic spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a scenic location people visit for the view.

clue.text: Fruit from the trees

parts.note: read not as apples or pears but as what grows out of a trunk: the branches

explanation.surface: Picking produce from an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Branches are the parts a tree puts forth, its outgrowths.

clue.text: Joint-stock holders?

parts.note: read not as company shareholders but as jugs holding the stock or juices that run from a roast joint

explanation.surface: Investors in a joint-stock company.
explanation.definitionFit: These jugs hold the sauce made from the juices of a roast joint of meat.

clue.text: The sort of desk that heads the list

parts.note: a roll is a list of names
to head something is to top it

explanation.surface: A type of desk that is the most popular.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of desk has a flexible slatted cover that slides up to open.

clue.text: Damage instrument with one note of the scale

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument
te is the seventh note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Ruining a musical instrument by playing one note.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate something is to harm or desecrate it.

clue.text: Supportive couple

parts.note: read both as a pair and as something that holds up or props

explanation.surface: Two partners who back each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, and also a strengthening support.

clue.text: Bowled over as we entered juggernaut

indicators.note: entered means went inside the word before

parts.note: a juggernaut is a very large lorry, a truck

explanation.surface: Knocked down when we drove into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A juggernaut is the British term for a huge articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amazed or overwhelmed is knocked back, filled with wonder.

clue.text: Neither the top nor bottom team

definitions.text: Neither the top nor bottom team

parts.words: Neither the top nor bottom team
parts.note: read as a league position, but really the vertical face between top and bottom, and a team

explanation.surface: A team in mid-table.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, and also the surface that is neither upper nor lower.

clue.text: They recommend a change of dress about six

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed letters wrap around the numeral
a change of means the word that follows is altered in arrangement

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Consultants suggest a different outfit for half a dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Advisers are people who give counsel or suggestions.

clue.text: I am a droll capering creature

indicators.note: capering means dancing about, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: An animal introduces itself as a comedian who likes to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas is a type of animal.

clue.text: Morning at last? Correct!

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the morning hours
at last means in the end, giving end

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether they are finally right that it is morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or put right a text or mistake.

clue.text: Made to sit around writing songs?

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the letters of the words beside it about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to stay seated while composing music.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Tosti was an Italian-born composer famous for parlour songs such as 'Goodbye'; 'Made' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosti was a composer celebrated for his drawing-room songs, so his name stands for someone writing them.

clue.text: Attempt to go without a singlet will lead to mockery

indicators.note: to go without here means to be placed on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a singlet is a vest, a sleeveless undergarment

explanation.surface: Trying to go out without an undershirt will make you a laughing stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go without' looks like doing without the singlet, but it means TRY goes around A VEST: TR(A VEST)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation that makes a mockery of something.

clue.text: Free silt I recycled at the river, for use on the farm

indicators.note: at places the river letter next to the anagram
recycled means processed again, the letters reshaped

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Recycling silt by a river to put on fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure and similar nutrients are spread on farmland to enrich the soil.

clue.text: Cause agitation, having fish and drink outside

indicators.note: outside means the drink word wraps around the fish word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble with fish and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake up a group is to disturb or reorganise it, causing upheaval.

clue.text: A cross government official I take out and carpet

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: take out means the named letter is removed

parts.note: a minister heads a government department

explanation.surface: An angry minister and I exit, and he tells me off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but it is X; 'carpet' as a noun is the definition, not a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of patterned woven rug, named after a Devon town.

clue.text: Wiping out a generation for certain

parts.note: a generation or age is an era
for certain means sure

explanation.surface: A whole generation is definitely going to be wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the act of rubbing out or obliterating something.

clue.text: Workers taking girl out in Spanish town

indicators.note: out here means outside, with the girl's name around the worker

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
worker ants are the classic crossword workers; one ant here

explanation.surface: Labourers taking a young woman out on a date in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a port city on the Costa Blanca in Spain.

clue.text: Slow cottoning on to the idea that part of the cosmos is doomed

definitions.text: Slow cottoning on to the idea

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters run inside the following words

explanation.surface: Gradually realising that some of the universe is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis figuratively means gradual, unconscious absorption of ideas.

clue.text: Spiced wine has fermentation of grain in it

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

parts.note: it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: fermentation means a churning, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mulled wine made from fermented grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and spices.

clue.text: Joint hazard in a wager

indicators.note: in places the hazard word inside the wager word

parts.note: a wager is a bet
a hazard is a risk

explanation.surface: A gamble on a weak knee or hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, a joint for roasting.

clue.text: The railway conveyed it — had an obligation to do so

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway

parts.words: had an obligation to do so
parts.note: ought means was obliged to

explanation.surface: The railway carried it, as it was obliged to.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the UK national rail operator until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought is the past tense of bring, meaning carried along.

clue.text: Recreation in nude? No! It's a malicious insinuation

indicators.note: read as re-creation: making the letters over again in a new order

explanation.surface: Refusing a suggestion of naturism as a pastime, since it is a smear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recreation' looks like leisure, but read as re-creation it reshuffles IN NUDE NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint, usually disparaging or suggestive.

clue.text: You said inflamed ring is nettle-rash

indicators.note: said tells us the word you is spoken and written as its soundalike letter

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U
inflamed skin is red
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone diagnoses an inflamed circle as hives.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a medical term for urticaria, an itchy skin eruption.

clue.text: Spirit changeless, though losing the game

indicators.note: losing means the game's letters are taken out of the word before

parts.note: chess is a well-known board game

explanation.surface: A spirit stays constant even after defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, H and E, S, S (CHESS, scattered) from CHANGELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit.

clue.text: Bird goes flying around in a circle

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go about the other piece
flying suggests the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: O is a circle

explanation.surface: A bird flies round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a large waterbird.

clue.text: Smart chap gets beer on credit initially

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A clever fellow buys his beer on tick.
explanation.walkthrough: A smart Alec is a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: This name forms the idiom for a clever-clogs or know-it-all.

clue.text: In travel it helps to be flexible

indicators.note: In tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Advice that suppleness is useful on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and bending easily.

clue.text: This rogue reformed — now no longer a rogue

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain has mended their ways and gone straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' does double duty in the surface (turned good) but in the parse just rearranges THIS ROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone virtuous and morally upright is no longer a villain.

clue.text: Seen in storm, an orc? Just birds!

indicators.note: seen in suggests the letters appear in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A monster glimpsed in a gale turns out to be only seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cormorants are large dark diving seabirds.

clue.text: Make approach to northern listener

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone moves towards a person from the north who will hear them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to come close to it.
